bull_bear.body: Strict 1/3 rule: 1/3 to dividends (₹5.00/share declared for FY26), 1/3 to business growth/working capital, 1/3 to capex. Considering share buyback as regulations ease.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical instability affecting exports; Delay in Indian government capex (Jal Jeevan/City Gas) impacting domestic volumes; Raw material (HR Coil) availability constraints; Execution risk on margin guidance given rising input costs.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic but defensive on past misses; Emphasizes 'conservative guidance' to avoid over-promising; Confident on FY27 being a 'record year' driven by exports; Transparent about labor/fuel headwinds.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Management explicitly lowered FY27 EBITDA/ton guidance (₹4,700) despite higher export mix, citing massive hidden cost inflation (labor/fuel) that peers may not be fully pricing in; The 'Middle East crisis' blocked 12k tons in Q4 but simultaneously accelerated the strategic pivot to the US market which offers double the EBITDA/ton.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Strengthening Financials – Net cash surplus of ₹ 337 crore as on 31st March 2026, Lean Balance Sheet"; consolidated "Investment in form of FDRs is ₹ 407 crore as of 31/03/2026" (Steel ₹375 crore, Lighting ₹32 crore).
- Consolidated debt has been cut sharply over five years: ₹580 crore (FY22), ₹404 crore (FY23), ₹4 crore (FY24), ₹3 crore (FY25), ₹65 crore (FY26); the Mar-26 balance sheet shows "Term Borrowings (incl. Current Maturities)" of nil and Working Capital Borrowings of ₹65 crore.
- Consolidated net worth has compounded steadily: ₹1,547 / 1,864 / 2,166 / 2,465 / 2,634 crore over FY22 to FY26.
- FY26 cash generation: net cash inflow from operating activities ₹400 crore (FY25: ₹394 crore) against investing outflow of ₹284 crore, leaving "Net cash flow from Operating & Investing activities" of ₹116 crore (FY25: ₹65 crore).
- Deck names dividend only inside a combined line — "Net cash (used in) / from financing activities, payment of interest, dividend and others" of ₹92 crore in FY26 versus ₹(80) crore in FY25 — and states no dividend amount, payout ratio or policy.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Steel: Q4 Rev ₹1,662 Cr, Vol 2.6 Lakh tons (record), EBITDA/ton ₹5,121. FY26 Vol 9.04 Lakh tons (+3% YoY), Value-added mix 43%. Lighting: Q4 Rev ₹501 Cr (+9% YoY), EBITDA ₹44 Cr (8.8% margin). FY26 Rev ₹1,809 Cr (+7% YoY). Wire & Cable: FY26 Rev ₹38 Cr, FY27 Target ₹260 Cr.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Raw material shortage and geopolitical export blocks suppressed volumes | APL Apollo Tubes | beneficiary | Med | Competitors reported strong Q4 while Surya missed; suggests peers better managed supply chain or had different export exposure. |
| Government capex delays in oil/gas/water sectors | Domestic Steel Pipe Peers | loser | Low | Sector-wide headwind, but Surya's higher exposure to tenders (15-30%) makes it relatively more vulnerable than pure retail-focused players. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Steel Pipes & Strips claims "#1 ERW GI Pipe manufacturer in India" and "#1 Exporter of ERW Pipes from India (50+ Countries)", with "50 Years of Brand presence in India, under the brand 'Prakash Surya'" (market positions stated to be "as per Management View").
- Lighting & Consumer Durables is positioned as "#2 Consumer Lighting Brand in India" and an "emerging FMEG Player", claiming leadership in AP, Telangana, MP, Chhattisgarh, Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand and second position in Karnataka, Delhi, Maharashtra, Bihar, Rajasthan and Uttarakhand.
- Distribution is presented as the core moat: "India's most deep rooted distribution network, major Revenue comes from Semi-urban and Rural markets" — 21,000+ pan-India dealers/retailers and 250+ distributors in steel, and "Over 3,00,000 Retail Outlets" plus "Secondary Network of 300+ RTF & 2,500+ DSPs" in lighting.
- Deck frames the strategy as "Strategic Value Creation by reinforcing market leadership position and driving change through investment in value-added products", with a stated aim to de-risk steel-price volatility by diversifying customer and product mix.
- Steel segment claims "Gained Market Share to ~10% of Oil & Gas Transmission Pipes" and holds "Accreditations from major PMC such as EIL, Mecon and others".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Government scheme — PLI] Commenced a manufacturing facility for LED components under the PLI scheme, "Large Investment" category; incentive quantum is "4% to 6% on sales over the base year for a period of five years subsequent to the base year", with the "claim of 3rd year received and also eligible for 4th year claim".
- [Brand] "onboarding of cricketer Suryakumar Yadav as the brand ambassador for its Steel Tubes & Pipes business".
- [Governance] Board includes Executive Chairman Shri J. P. Agarwal (Padma Shri awardee) and two Managing Directors — Shri Raju Bista (past President of ELCOMA, presently a Member of Parliament) and Shri Vinay Surya.
- [Demand policy hooks] Steel demand case rests on government programmes — "Government thrust on high investments, CGD, Smart Cities, Nal se Jal" with "₹ 5 lac crore investment expected in 5 years"; PVC pipes cite "Housing for All, 'Nal se Jal', Project AMRUT and Swachh Bharat Mission" and a sector "expected to see an average Annual growth of 10%".
- [Recognition] Named among "Top 500 Value Creators 2025"; Ms. Puja Surya recognised as an Industry Leader by Economic Times for "Excellence in Integrated Manufacturing and Supply Chain".
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Pressure from new labor laws (₹30-40 Cr impact), rising fuel/power costs, and imported raw materials for Lighting (30-35% import content). Domestic API/tender margins compressed due to competition; offset by high-margin US exports.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: ~24-25% for FY27 (Target ₹9,400-9,500 Cr). Margin: Steel EBITDA/ton guided at ~₹4,700 (down from Q4's ₹5,121 due to cost pressures); Consolidated EBITDA target ₹680-700 Cr. Order Inflow: Strong visibility from US exports (65k tons booked). Capex/Commissioning: Capacity to reach 1.6 Mn tons in FY27; 1.9 Mn tons by FY29.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Steel Division: ₹1,000+ Crores (led by exports, spiral, domestic API); Lighting Division: ₹160 Crores (Professional Lighting).
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: North America export pivot (targeting 2.5 Lakh tons in FY27 vs 1.36 Lakh tons in FY26 with ₹9k-10k/ton EBITDA); Capacity expansion to 1.9 Mn tons by FY29; Wire & Cable scaling to ₹500-600 Cr run-rate; Potential demerger of Lighting business.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Surya Roshni navigated a volatile Q4FY26 marked by Middle East export disruptions and domestic raw material shortages, resulting in flat revenue and compressed margins, but management guides for a record FY27 driven by a strategic pivot to high-margin North American exports and capacity expansion. The key inflection is the shift from reliance on volatile domestic government tenders to secured, high-realization export orders which are expected to offset domestic margin compression from labor/fuel costs.

themes.title: Steel tubes & building-materials capex beneficiaries
themes.need: Domestic capex + import-substitution lift value-added steel tubes/pipes and building materials - APLAPOLLO/HITECH/JTLIND/SURYAROSNI/SAMBHV/VENUSPIPES on structural & SS tubes (solar structures, DC cooling, API), FINPIPE/SUPREMEIND/APOLLOPIPE on PVC pipes, MAANALU on aluminium extrusions, RATNAVEER on SS fasteners. A data-center-cooling adjacency adds margin optionality.
themes.driver: Capex commissioning converting to volume; solar-structure & infra demand; commodity pass-through.
